summary: Intermittent 429 bursts during multi-key client surge — cross-tenant quota interaction
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent bursts of 429 responses when their ingestion clients perform short-lived parallel uploads across multiple API keys. The behavior appears correlated with short traffic surges (few seconds) where the overall per-account quota is not exceeded, but per-API-key token buckets and a shared cross-tenant surge policy cause transient 429s.

Impact:
- Multiple ingestion jobs report spikes of 20-40% 429s for 10-30s windows every ~6-12 hours.
- Affects latency-sensitive pipelines (embedding and reranking) and causes retries that increase downstream costs.
- Customer is on a dedicated pool; they expect stable throughput with low jitter.

Context/why this is unusual:
- Total tokens during spikes remain under the committed reserved capacity for the dedicated pool.
- 429s correlate to API key-level bucket exhaustion and a conservative global surge policy that tries to protect noisy neighbors by imposing short back-offs across all keys in a shared proxy shard.

Customer notes:
- They run multiple ephemeral worker instances each with its own API key (rotating per process) to parallelize work.
- When workers rotate keys, the bursts line up and exceed per-key burst windows even though aggregate usage is within expected range.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer runs 200 short requests/sec for 15s using 40 unique API keys across a single dedicated pool.
2) Observe per-key token consumption and overall pool metrics via console.
3) After ~8-12s, API returns 429s from the shared proxy layer for several seconds.
4) Retry logic with immediate exponential backoff leads to elevated token usage and repeat bursts.

Note: Repro is most reliable when keys are rotated rapidly and when requests are short and bursty (avg payload 512 tokens).
logs:
Sample logs (api-gateway):
[2026-03-10T14:07:11.329Z] key=key-17 shard=sproxy-3 route=/v1/generate status=429 reason=per_key_burst_exceeded remaining=0
[2026-03-10T14:07:11.331Z] key=key-22 shard=sproxy-3 route=/v1/generate status=429 reason=surge_policy_throttle window_ms=500
[2026-03-10T14:07:11.402Z] key=key-05 shard=sproxy-3 route=/v1/embedding status=200 consumed_tokens=120
[2026-03-10T14:07:13.145Z] quota-service: shard=sproxy-3 aggregate_account_tokens=8420 committed_capacity=10000

Observations: per_key buckets show zeros even when aggregate_account_tokens < committed_capacity.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: conservative surge policy in shared proxy shard is applying per-shard backpressure on top of per-key buckets, causing 429s despite free reserved capacity.
Actions taken:
- Pulled rate-limiter metrics for sproxy-3 (latency, leaky bucket levels, refill rates).
- Correlated API key rotation events from the customer's telemetry with 429 spikes.
- Checked dedicated pool autoscaling logs — no scaling events during spikes.
- Validated that the customer's account commit (10k tokens/min) was not exceeded.

Findings:
- Per-key token bucket configuration: burst_capacity small (3x baseline) and refill granularity coarse (1s).
- Shared proxy surge_policy: when a shard sees concurrent per-key exhaustions it applies a short global window_ms=500 throttle to reduce amplification; this was tuned for shared multi-tenant pools and is extra-conservative for dedicated pools behind shared proxies.
- SDKs from the customer lacked jittered randomized backoff on immediate retries, amplifying bursts.

Hypothesis validated: combination of small per-key burst windows + shared-proxy surge policy + synchronized key rotation => transient 429s even for committed dedicated capacity.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) [2026-03-10]: Reproduced with customer payload locally using their key rotation pattern. Escalating to SRE for surge policy review.

SRE (Jonah Reyes) [2026-03-11]: Confirmed surge_policy is enabled on sproxy-3. For dedicated customers we normally gate surge_policy at the pool boundary but this customer's traffic flows through older shared proxy config. Investigating rollback options.
Customer (NimbleSearch) [2026-03-11]: We can modify key rotation frequency if needed, but preferred long-term fix is to avoid 429s at our committed capacity. Also open to SDK backoff guidance.

Engine (Maya Li) [2026-03-11]: Proposed two fixes: 1) increase per-key burst_capacity for this account; 2) disable shard-level surge_policy for sproxy-3 for this dedicated pool until global fix lands. Both require risk assessment.

SRE (Jonah Reyes) [2026-03-12]: Implemented temporary mitigation: bumped per-key burst_capacity for NimbleSearch API keys from 3x -> 10x and added a 250ms randomized backoff at the proxy to smooth arrival. Monitoring shows 429s dropped to <1% during a controlled 30-minute run.
Support (Aisha) [2026-03-12]: Sent recommended SDK backoff patch to NimbleSearch and documentation snippet for token-bucket best practices.
resolution:
Mitigation applied 2026-03-12: temporary per-key burst increase and proxy-side randomized smoothing.
Permanent plan:
- Engineering to deploy PR #4523 to adjust surge_policy logic: for dedicated pools behind shared proxy, consult pool_commit values before applying shard-level global windows.
- Update default per-key burst config for customers using key-rotation patterns (target: burst_capacity configurable by pool admin).
- Publish SDK guidance on jittered backoffs and recommended key rotation cadence.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-8142 (work item) created to make surge_policy pool-aware and add a feature flag.
- Notify product to add an option in Console to override per-key burst for accounts on dedicated pools.

Customer impact: resolved (customer confirmed drop in 429s and stable ingest).
